zone.no_metrics: No metrics mapped for this zone yet.

forecast.unsupported: Forecasts are not supported by this weather entity.

validation.alert_entity_required: Alert {alert} has a condition without an entity.
validation.alert_entity_not_found: Entity {entity} configured for alert {alert} was not found.

metrics.outdoor_temperature: Current outdoor air temperature measured by the weather station or sensor.
metrics.apparent_temperature: Perceived outdoor temperature accounting for wind chill and humidity (feels like temperature).
metrics.humidity: Outdoor relative humidity shows how close the air is to saturation at its current temperature. Because warm air can contain more water vapor than cold air, use absolute humidity when comparing indoor and outdoor moisture.
metrics.pressure: Atmospheric pressure measured by the station. Weather interpretations such as low or high pressure are meaningful for sea-level-corrected values; raw station pressure also depends strongly on altitude.
metrics.wind_speed: Current sustained wind speed observed at the station.
metrics.wind_bearing: Direction from which the wind is blowing, expressed in degrees or compass points.
metrics.wind_gust: Peak wind speed measured during recent gusts.
metrics.precipitation: Current precipitation intensity or accumulated rainfall.
metrics.precipitation_probability: Likelihood of precipitation occurring in the forecast period.
metrics.uv_index: Ultraviolet radiation index: 0–2 is low, 3–5 moderate, 6–7 high, 8–10 very high and 11+ extreme. Protection becomes increasingly important as the value rises.
metrics.visibility: Distance at which objects can be clearly seen under current atmospheric conditions.
metrics.dew_point: The temperature at which the air would reach 100% relative humidity and water could condense. A high dew point feels muggy; indoors, any surface colder than the dew point can collect condensation.
metrics.cloud_coverage: Percentage of sky covered by clouds.
metrics.ozone: Ozone reported by the selected source. Depending on its unit, this may represent local ground-level concentration or total atmospheric ozone, so interpret it with the integration documentation.
metrics.air_quality: Overall air quality index based on pollutant levels. The scale and health bands depend on the integration and country standard providing the value.
metrics.sunrise: Time of sunrise at your location.
metrics.sunset: Time of sunset at your location.

zone_metric.temperature: Ambient air temperature measured in this zone.
zone_metric.humidity: Relative humidity measured in this zone. About 40–60% is commonly comfortable indoors, but the configured comfort thresholds remain authoritative for this card.
zone_metric.aqi: Air quality index: a combined indicator of pollutant levels and possible health effects. Its scale varies by provider, so compare it with the bands used by your sensor.
zone_metric.co2: Carbon dioxide concentration in parts per million (ppm). Indoor levels above 1000 ppm may indicate poor ventilation.
zone_metric.pm2_5: Fine particles smaller than 2.5 micrometers that can travel deep into the lungs. Lower values are better; use your local health authority's thresholds for action.
zone_metric.pm10: Particles smaller than 10 micrometers that can irritate the airways. Lower values are better; interpretation depends on the averaging period and local standard.
zone_metric.voc: Volatile organic compounds released by products, cooking and materials. The sensor may report a concentration or a relative index, so use its own scale and baseline.

comfort.outdoor_summary: Overall outdoor comfort assessment based on temperature and humidity.
comfort.saturation_distance: Outdoor temperature minus dew point. A small margin means the air is close to saturation and dew or fog is more likely; a large margin means it is drier relative to saturation.
comfort.absolute_humidity: Mass of water vapor per cubic meter of air. Comparing indoor and outdoor absolute humidity is more useful for ventilation than comparing relative humidity at two different temperatures.
comfort.dew_point_outdoor: Temperature at which outdoor air reaches 100% humidity and moisture condenses.
comfort.dew_point_indoor: Temperature at which indoor air reaches saturation. Surfaces colder than this risk condensation.
comfort.condensation_margin: Window surface temperature minus indoor dew point. At or below 0°C margin, condensation is likely; 0–3°C is a warning buffer, and more than 3°C is a safer margin.
comfort.ventilation: Compares indoor and outdoor absolute humidity. Opening windows can remove moisture when outdoor air contains sufficiently less water vapor, but this display does not account for pollution, security or noise.
comfort.cooling: Checks whether the room is above your comfort maximum and outdoor air is cooler by the configured difference. It does not account for wind, solar gains or air quality.
comfort.surface_temperature: Window or surface temperature used for condensation analysis. A sensor is treated as measured; without one, the displayed estimate uses indoor/outdoor temperatures and your glazing factor.

sun.azimuth: Compass direction of the sun, measured clockwise from true north (0° = north, 90° = east, 180° = south, 270° = west).
sun.elevation: Angle of the sun above the horizon. 0° sits on the horizon, 90° is straight overhead; negative values mean the sun is below the horizon.
sun.solar_noon: The moment the sun is highest and crosses the local meridian — usually not exactly 12:00 clock time, because of your longitude within the timezone and the equation of time.
sun.day_length: Time between sunrise and sunset today at your location.

comfort.ventilation_open: Open windows — outdoor air is drier
comfort.ventilation_avoid: Keep windows closed — outdoor air is more humid
comfort.cooling_open: Open windows — outdoor air is cooler
comfort.cooling_avoid: Windows won't help — outdoor is not cool enough
comfort.cooling_unnecessary: No cooling needed — temperature is comfortable

sun.polar_day: Polar day — the sun stays above the horizon all day
sun.polar_night: Polar night — the sun stays below the horizon all day
sun.unavailable: Set your Home Assistant location (latitude/longitude) to show the sun path.

editor.title: Card title
editor.title_helper: Optional title displayed at the top of the card.
editor.weather_entity_helper: Leave empty to auto-detect the best weather entity.
editor.mapping_helper: For every outdoor station metric, this tab shows exactly which entity/attribute is currently used and lets you type any entity id to override it manually. A manual override always wins over automatic detection. Start typing to see compatible entities, then clear the field to go back to automatic detection.
editor.image_url_helper: Use a /local/… path (files in config/www) or an HTTPS URL. The image must contain a transparent sky (alpha channel).
editor.image_fit_helper: Use “Show the entire image” to remove automatic cropping. The animated sky fills any remaining space.
editor.min_height_helper: Minimum height of the animated scene viewport only (sky/house/precipitation). The information area below always grows naturally with its content and is never clipped.
editor.aspect_ratio_helper: Optional aspect ratio applied to the scene viewport only (e.g. 16/9). Leave empty to only use the minimum height.
editor.metrics_helper: Choose which station metrics are visible, their order, label, color and icon. To change which entity feeds a metric, use the "Entity mapping" tab.
editor.auto_configure_confirm: Auto-configure will save the automatically detected weather entity and sensors into this card's configuration. Continue?
editor.environment_helper: Add unlimited indoor and/or outdoor zones (rooms, garage, garden…) with manually mapped entities. Zone assignment is always manual and reliable — there is no automatic guessing of which room a sensor belongs to.
editor.remove_zone_confirm: Remove this environment zone? This cannot be undone.
editor.alerts_helper: Build visual recommendation rules (e.g. "Open the windows") from one or more numeric conditions. These are display-only: they are only evaluated while this card is open in your browser, and never call Home Assistant services, automations or notifications.
editor.alerts_example: Example: name "Open windows", conditions indoor CO₂ greater than 1000 ppm AND outdoor air quality index less than 50 AND outdoor temperature between 12 and 28.
editor.remove_alert_confirm: Remove this recommendation rule? This cannot be undone.
editor.comfort_helper: Analyses indoor comfort by comparing outdoor and indoor temperature and humidity. Provides ventilation and natural cooling advice. No home automation is triggered.
editor.comfort_disclaimer: Recommendations are indicative only and based on thermodynamic estimates. Always use your own judgement.
editor.comfort_indoor_zone_helper: Leave empty to use the first visible indoor zone automatically.
editor.comfort_surface_entity_helper: If left empty, the surface temperature is estimated from indoor and outdoor temperatures using the glazing factor. When provided, the measured value is used instead.
editor.comfort_surface_invalid: Entity not found. Check the entity id.
editor.comfort_glazing_factor_helper: Approximate fraction of the outdoor–indoor temperature difference used to estimate the inner window surface. Indicative center-pane ranges: high-performance glazing 0.08–0.12, modern double glazing 0.14–0.20, older double glazing 0.25–0.40, single glazing 0.60–0.75. Frames, edges, wind and installation can differ greatly; use a surface sensor for reliable assessment.
editor.sun_helper: Shows the sun's daily arc (sunrise, solar noon, sunset), its current azimuth and elevation, the day length and the season — all computed locally from your Home Assistant location, with no network calls.
